scenes.section: A barcode for every medicine pack

lines.raw: On medical claims, CPT procedure codes act as the "barcodes" of services (the Medical course covers them).
lines.say: On medical claims, C P T procedure codes act as the "barcodes" of services (the Medical course covers them).

lines.raw: For medicines, the barcode is the **NDC (National Drug Code)**.
lines.say: For medicines, the barcode is the N D C (National Drug Code).

lines.raw: It is printed on every US medicine box and bottle, and it is the **most important field** on a pharmacy claim: it says exactly **which drug** was dispensed.
lines.say: It is printed on every U S medicine box and bottle, and it is the most important field on a pharmacy claim: it says exactly which drug was dispensed.

scenes.section: A barcode for every medicine pack

lines.raw: Think of a Wai Wai noodle packet.
lines.say: Think of a Wai Wai noodle packet.

lines.raw: One packet, a box of 30 packets and a different flavour all have **different barcodes**, even though they are made by the same company.
lines.say: One packet, a box of 30 packets and a different flavour all have different barcodes, even though they are made by the same company.

lines.raw: NDCs work the same way: the **company**, the **product** (drug, strength and form) and the **pack size** each change the code.
lines.say: N D C's work the same way: the company, the product (drug, strength and form) and the pack size each change the code.

lines.raw: Three parts.
lines.say: Three parts.

lines.raw: A 10-digit NDC (illustrative).
lines.say: A 10-digit N D C (illustrative).

lines.raw: 12345: **Labeler**: the company that makes, repackages or distributes the drug.
lines.say: 12345: Labeler: the company that makes, repackages or distributes the drug.

lines.raw: The **FDA** assigns this code.
lines.say: The F D A assigns this code.

lines.raw: 101: **Product**: the drug, its **strength** and **dosage form**.
lines.say: 101: Product: the drug, its strength and dosage form.

lines.raw: Here: amoxicillin **500 mg capsules**.
lines.say: Here: amoxicillin 500 mg capsules.

lines.raw: The company chooses this code.
lines.say: The company chooses this code.

lines.raw: 05: **Package**: the pack size and type.
lines.say: 05: Package: the pack size and type.

lines.raw: Here: a bottle of 500 capsules.
lines.say: Here: a bottle of 500 capsules.

lines.raw: The company chooses this code too.
lines.say: The company chooses this code too.

lines.raw: Example NDCs in this course are made up.
lines.say: Example N D C's in this course are made up.

lines.raw: To keep things simple, the NDCs used for Emily's medicines are **illustrative**, not real products.
lines.say: To keep things simple, the N D C's used for Emily's medicines are illustrative, not real products.

lines.raw: To look up a real NDC, use the free **FDA NDC Directory**.
lines.say: To look up a real N D C, use the free F D A N D C Directory.

lines.raw: Same medicine, many NDCs.
lines.say: Same medicine, many N D C's.

lines.raw: Amoxicillin 500 mg is made by many companies, so it has many **labeler** codes.
lines.say: Amoxicillin 500 mg is made by many companies, so it has many labeler codes.

lines.raw: Each company sells several **pack sizes** (30, 100, 500 capsules), so each has several **package** codes.
lines.say: Each company sells several pack sizes (30, 100, 500 capsules), so each has several package codes.

lines.raw: One drug can easily have **dozens of NDCs**.
lines.say: One drug can easily have dozens of N D C's.

lines.raw: The pharmacy reports the NDC of the bottle it **actually took the capsules from**.
lines.say: The pharmacy reports the N D C of the bottle it actually took the capsules from.

lines.raw: Three 10-digit shapes.
lines.say: Three 10-digit shapes.

lines.raw: The FDA gives out NDCs as **10 digits** in three parts, but the parts can have different lengths.
lines.say: The F D A gives out N D C's as 10 digits in three parts, but the parts can have different lengths.

lines.raw: There are three shapes:
lines.say: There are three shapes:

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **4-4-2**. Labeler: 4 digits. Product: 4 digits. Package: 2 digits. Example: `2345-6789-01`.
lines.say: 4-4-2. Labeler: 4 digits. Product: 4 digits. Package: 2 digits. Example: 2 3 4 5 dash 6 7 8 9 dash 0 1.

lines.raw: **5-3-2**. Labeler: 5 digits. Product: 3 digits. Package: 2 digits. Example: `12345-101-05`.
lines.say: 5-3-2. Labeler: 5 digits. Product: 3 digits. Package: 2 digits. Example: 1 2 3 4 5 dash 1 0 1 dash 0 5.

lines.raw: **5-4-1**. Labeler: 5 digits. Product: 4 digits. Package: 1 digit. Example: `34567-0220-9`.
lines.say: 5-4-1. Labeler: 5 digits. Product: 4 digits. Package: 1 digit. Example: 3 4 5 6 7 dash 0 2 2 0 dash 9.

lines.raw: This is a problem for computers: without the dashes, `2345678901` and `1234510105` look the same length but are split differently.
lines.say: This is a problem for computers: without the dashes, 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 0 1 and 1 2 3 4 5 1 0 1 0 5 look the same length but are split differently.

lines.raw: So claims and data files use **one fixed shape**: **11 digits, 5-4-2**.
lines.say: So claims and data files use one fixed shape: 11 digits, 5-4-2.

lines.raw: To get there, you add **one leading zero** to the part that is **too short**.
lines.say: To get there, you add one leading zero to the part that is too short.

lines.raw: Converting 10 digits to 11 digits (5-4-2).
lines.say: Converting 10 digits to 11 digits (5-4-2).

lines.raw: 4-4-2. 10-digit NDC: `2345-6789-01`. Where the zero goes: Front of the **labeler**. 11-digit (5-4-2): `02345-6789-01`. Stored in data: `02345678901`.
lines.say: 4-4-2. 10-digit N D C: 2 3 4 5 dash 6 7 8 9 dash 0 1. Where the zero goes: Front of the labeler. 11-digit (5-4-2): 0 2 3 4 5 dash 6 7 8 9 dash 0 1. Stored in data: 0 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 0 1.

lines.raw: 5-3-2. 10-digit NDC: `12345-101-05`. Where the zero goes: Front of the **product**. 11-digit (5-4-2): `12345-0101-05`. Stored in data: `12345010105`.
lines.say: 5-3-2. 10-digit N D C: 1 2 3 4 5 dash 1 0 1 dash 0 5. Where the zero goes: Front of the product. 11-digit (5-4-2): 1 2 3 4 5 dash 0 1 0 1 dash 0 5. Stored in data: 1 2 3 4 5 0 1 0 1 0 5.

lines.raw: 5-4-1. 10-digit NDC: `34567-0220-9`. Where the zero goes: Front of the **package**. 11-digit (5-4-2): `34567-0220-09`. Stored in data: `34567022009`.
lines.say: 5-4-1. 10-digit N D C: 3 4 5 6 7 dash 0 2 2 0 dash 9. Where the zero goes: Front of the package. 11-digit (5-4-2): 3 4 5 6 7 dash 0 2 2 0 dash 0 9. Stored in data: 3 4 5 6 7 0 2 2 0 0 9.

lines.raw: The same amoxicillin NDC in 11-digit form.
lines.say: The same amoxicillin N D C in 11-digit form.

lines.raw: 12345: Labeler: **5 digits** (already 5, no change).
lines.say: 12345: Labeler: 5 digits (already 5, no change).

lines.raw: 0101: Product: was `101`, a **zero added in front** to make 4 digits.
lines.say: 0101: Product: was 101, a zero added in front to make 4 digits.

lines.raw: 05: Package: **2 digits** (already 2, no change).
lines.say: 05: Package: 2 digits (already 2, no change).

lines.raw: You need the dashes to convert.
lines.say: You need the dashes to convert.

lines.raw: You can only convert safely if you know **where the dashes were**.
lines.say: You can only convert safely if you know where the dashes were.

lines.raw: A plain 10-digit number without dashes cannot be converted reliably, because you cannot tell which part is short.
lines.say: A plain 10-digit number without dashes cannot be converted reliably, because you cannot tell which part is short.

lines.raw: That is why data teams convert once, at the start, and then **always store the 11-digit form without dashes**.
lines.say: That is why data teams convert once, at the start, and then always store the 11-digit form without dashes.

lines.raw: Store NDCs as text, never as numbers.
lines.say: Store N D C's as text, never as numbers.

scenes.section: Store NDCs as text, never as numbers

lines.raw: If you save it as a **number**, a spreadsheet or database quietly drops the leading zero and you get `2345678901`: only 10 digits, and now it matches **nothing**.
lines.say: If you save it as a number, a spreadsheet or database quietly drops the leading zero and you get 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 0 1: only 10 digits, and now it matches nothing.

lines.raw: Joins to drug reference tables fail and the drug disappears from your report.
lines.say: Joins to drug reference tables fail and the drug disappears from your report.

scenes.section: Store NDCs as text, never as numbers

lines.raw: Store NDC in a **text** column (for example `VARCHAR(11)` or `CHAR(11)`).
lines.say: Store N D C in a text column (for example V A R C H A R ( 1 1 ) or C H A R ( 1 1 )).

lines.raw: Always **11 digits**, **no dashes**, **leading zeros kept**.
lines.say: Always 11 digits, no dashes, leading zeros kept.

lines.raw: When opening a file in Excel, import the NDC column as **Text**, or the zeros vanish.
lines.say: When opening a file in Excel, import the N D C column as Text, or the zeros vanish.

lines.raw: If you find a 10-digit or 9-digit NDC in data, it has probably lost its zeros.
lines.say: If you find a 10-digit or 9-digit N D C in data, it has probably lost its zeros.

lines.raw: Pad it back with zeros on the left to 11 digits, and check it against a reference list.
lines.say: Pad it back with zeros on the left to 11 digits, and check it against a reference list.

scenes.section: Store NDCs as text, never as numbers

lines.say: The same thing happens to other codes with leading zeros, like revenue codes (0 2 5 0) and U S Z I P codes (0 2 1 3 4).

lines.raw: Codes are **labels**, not amounts.
lines.say: Codes are labels, not amounts.

lines.raw: You never add them up, so store them as text.
lines.say: You never add them up, so store them as text.

lines.raw: Analysts rarely ask "how many fills of NDC `34567022009`?" They ask "how many fills of **atorvastatin**?" or "how much did we spend on **cholesterol medicines**?" To answer, they join the NDC to a **drug reference table** that groups NDCs:
lines.say: Analysts rarely ask "how many fills of N D C 3 4 5 6 7 0 2 2 0 0 9?" They ask "how many fills of atorvastatin?" or "how much did we spend on cholesterol medicines?" To answer, they join the N D C to a drug reference table that groups N D C's:

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **RxNorm** (RXCUI). What it is: A free drug vocabulary from the US **National Library of Medicine**. Links NDCs to ingredient, strength and form. Use it to answer: All fills of atorvastatin 20 mg tablets, from any company.
lines.say: RxNorm (R X C U I). What it is: A free drug vocabulary from the U S National Library of Medicine. Links N D C's to ingredient, strength and form. Use it to answer: All fills of atorvastatin 20 mg tablets, from any company.

lines.raw: **GPI** (Generic Product Identifier). What it is: A **14-character** code from a commercial drug database. Read left to right, it goes from broad group to exact drug, form and strength. Use it to answer: All cholesterol medicines, then all statins, then atorvastatin.
lines.say: G P I (Generic Product Identifier). What it is: A 14-character code from a commercial drug database. Read left to right, it goes from broad group to exact drug, form and strength. Use it to answer: All cholesterol medicines, then all statins, then atorvastatin.

lines.raw: **Therapeutic class**. What it is: A category by what the drug treats or how it works. Use it to answer: Antibiotics, statins, pain relievers.
lines.say: Therapeutic class. What it is: A category by what the drug treats or how it works. Use it to answer: Antibiotics, statins, pain relievers.
